questions.question: The problem of myopia in human eye can be corrected by using:

options.text: a biconvex lens of suitable power
a concave lens of suitable power
a convex lens of suitable power

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a concave lens of suitable power**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Myopia, also known as nearsightedness, is a common vision condition where close objects appear clear, but distant objects are blurry.
 
• This condition occurs when the eye is too long relative to the focusing power of the cornea and lens of the eye.
 
• As a result, light rays focus at a point in front of the retina rather than directly on its surface.
 
• A concave lens (diverging lens) is used to correct myopia by diverging light rays before they enter the eye, allowing them to focus on the retina.
 
• The power of the concave lens is chosen based on the degree of myopia, ensuring that the light is focused correctly on the retina for clear vision.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hyperopia (Farsightedness)**

 
 
• In hyperopia, distant objects can be seen more clearly than close ones.
 
• This condition is corrected using a convex lens (converging lens) to focus light correctly on the retina.
 
 
 
• **Astigmatism**
 
 
• Astigmatism is a condition where the cornea or lens is irregularly shaped, causing blurred or distorted vision.
 
• It can be corrected with cylindrical lenses that compensate for the irregular shape of the cornea or lens.
 
 
 
• **Presbyopia**
 
 
• Presbyopia is an age-related condition where the eye's lens loses its flexibility, making it difficult to focus on close objects.
 
• This condition is typically corrected with reading glasses or bifocals.

questions.question: The distance between the pole and focus of a spherical mirror, in terms of its radius of curvature R, is equal to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**R/2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The distance between the pole and the focus of a spherical mirror is known as the focal length (f).
 
• The radius of curvature (R) is the distance between the pole and the center of curvature of the mirror.
 
• The focal length of a spherical mirror is half of its radius of curvature.
 
• Mathematically, this relationship is expressed as f=(R)/(2)
 
• This applies to both concave and convex mirrors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirrors**

 
 
• These mirrors curve inward like a spoon and can form real or virtual images depending on the position of the object.
 
• They are often used in applications like telescopes and shaving mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Convex Mirrors**
 
 
• These mirrors curve outward and always form virtual, diminished, and upright images.
 
• They are commonly used as rear-view mirrors in vehicles.
 
 
 
• **Mirror Formula**
 
 
• The mirror equation (1)/(f)=(1)/(v)+(1)/(u) relates the focal length (f), image distance (v), and object distance (u) for spherical mirrors.
 
• This formula is applicable to both concave and convex mirrors.

questions.question: Which of the following solutions is identified by smell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dettol in water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dettol is a well-known antiseptic liquid that has a distinctive smell, making it easily identifiable.
 
• The smell of Dettol is due to the presence of chloroxylenol, which is its active ingredient.
 
• When Dettol is dissolved in water, its characteristic smell remains, allowing it to be identified by olfactory senses.
 
• Other solutions like sugar in water, salt in water, and potassium permanganate in water do not have a strong smell, making them harder to identify by smell alone.
 
• Dettol is commonly used for cleaning and disinfecting surfaces, as well as for first aid purposes due to its antiseptic properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Salt in Water**

 
 
• Salt (sodium chloride) dissolved in water does not have any significant odor.
 
• It is commonly used in cooking and food preservation.
 
 
 
• **Sugar in Water**
 
 
• Sugar dissolved in water is sweet to taste but does not have any specific smell.
 
• It is widely used in beverages and culinary preparations.
 
 
 
• **Potassium Permanganate in Water**
 
 
• Potassium permanganate in water has a pink or purple color, but it does not have a strong smell.
 
• It is often used as a disinfectant and in water treatment processes.

questions.question: Which of the following formulas is used to calculate the volume by volume percentage of a solution?

options.text: frac{{Mass of solute}}{{Volume of solution}} times 100
frac{{Mass of solute}}{{Mass of solution}} times 100
frac{{Volume of solute}}{{Volume of solution}} times 100
frac{{Volume of solution}}{{Mass of solute}} times 100

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Volume of solute / Volume of solution × 100**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Volume by volume percentage (v/v %)** is used to express the concentration of a solution when both the **solute** and the **solution** are measured in terms of **volume**.
 
• The formula for calculating volume by volume percentage is:

 **Volume by Volume % = (Volume of solute / Volume of solution) × 100**
 
• In this formula:
 
 
• **Volume of solute** = Amount of substance dissolved.
 
• **Volume of solution** = Total volume after mixing solute and solvent.
 
 
 
• This method is commonly used for **liquid-liquid solutions**, such as **alcohol in water**.
 
• **Option-wise Analysis:**
 
 
• **Mass of solute / Volume of solution × 100** – Used for mass by volume percentage, not v/v percentage.
 
• **Mass of solute / Mass of solution × 100** – Used for mass by mass percentage.
 
• **Volume of solute / Volume of solution × 100** – **Correct**.
 
• **Volume of solution / Mass of solute × 100** – Incorrect formula.
 
 
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Volume of solute / Volume of solution × 100.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mass by Mass Percentage (w/w %):**

 **(Mass of solute / Mass of solution) × 100**
 
• **Mass by Volume Percentage (w/v %):**

 **(Mass of solute / Volume of solution) × 100**
 
• **Molarity:** Number of moles of solute dissolved per litre of solution.
 
• **Solute:** The substance that gets dissolved in a solvent.
 
• **Solvent:** The substance that dissolves the solute to form a solution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Example:** If **20 mL** alcohol is mixed to make **100 mL** solution, then:

 **v/v % = (20 / 100) × 100 = 20%**
 
• Volume percentage is widely used in **pharmaceuticals, beverages, perfumes, and chemical industries**.

questions.question: A ball of mass 0.5 kg is thrown vertically upwards and rises to a height of 20 m. The approximate initial velocity of the ball is:
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

**Equations of Motion under Gravity:**

__
 
• The motion of objects under the influence of gravity can be described using the equations of motion.
 
• For an object thrown vertically upward, the final velocity at the highest point is zero.
 
• Formula: v² = u² + 2as
 
• Here, **v** is the final velocity, **u** is the initial velocity, **a** is acceleration (due to gravity), and **s** is the displacement.
 
• **Acceleration due to gravity (g):** The acceleration imparted to objects due to the gravitational force. SI unit: m/s². Dimensional Formula: [LT⁻²]. g ≈ 9.8 m/s².

**Calculation:**__

Given,

Mass of the ball, m = 0.5 kg (Not required for calculation)

Maximum height, s = 20 m

Final velocity at the highest point, v = 0 m/s

Acceleration due to gravity, a = -9.8 m/s² (negative as it is upward motion)

Using the equation of motion:

v² = u² + 2as

Substitute the given values:

0 = u² + 2(-9.8)(20)

⇒ 0 = u² - 392

⇒ u² = 392

⇒ u = sqrt{392}

⇒ u ≈ 19.8 {m/s}

**∴ The initial velocity of the ball is approximately 20 m/s.**

questions.question: Which of the following is a cup-shaped part of nephron with which each capillary cluster in the kidney is associated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bowman's capsule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bowman's capsule is a cup-shaped structure that encases the glomerulus in the nephron of the kidney.
 
• It is the first part of the nephron where the filtration of blood takes place to form urine.
 
• The Bowman's capsule collects the filtrate from the glomerulus and channels it into the proximal convoluted tubule.
 
• The structure of the Bowman's capsule allows it to efficiently filter blood plasma while preventing the passage of blood cells and large proteins.
 
• The interaction between the Bowman's capsule and the glomerulus is crucial for the kidney's function of removing waste and excess substances from the bloodstream.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Proximal Convoluted Tubule**

 
 
• This is the section of the nephron that follows the Bowman's capsule.
 
• It is responsible for the reabsorption of water, ions, and nutrients back into the bloodstream.
 
 
 
• **Distal Convoluted Tubule**
 
 
• This is the portion of the nephron that follows the loop of Henle.
 
• It is involved in the regulation of potassium, sodium, calcium, and pH balance in the body.
 
 
 
• **Glomerulus**
 
 
• A network of capillaries located within the Bowman's capsule.
 
• It is responsible for the filtration of blood to form the initial urine filtrate.

questions.question: The _____ moves water and minerals obtained from the soil while ______ transports products of photosynthesis from the leaves where they are synthesised to other parts of the plant.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**xylem, phloem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Xylem** is responsible for the transport of water and minerals from the roots to other parts of the plant.
 
• **Phloem** is responsible for the transport of the products of photosynthesis, primarily sugars, from the leaves to other parts of the plant.
 
• Xylem consists of vessels and tracheids, which are tubular structures that facilitate the upward movement of water and minerals.
 
• Phloem consists of sieve tubes and companion cells, which work together to transport nutrients throughout the plant.
 
• The process of water transport in xylem is largely driven by transpiration and root pressure, whereas phloem transport is driven by the pressure-flow mechanism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Collenchyma**

 
 
• It is a type of plant tissue that provides support and flexibility to growing parts of the plant such as stems and leaves.
 
• Collenchyma cells have thicker cell walls compared to parenchyma cells and are often found under the epidermis.
 
 
 
• **Parenchyma**
 
 
• It is the most common type of plant tissue, involved in various functions including photosynthesis, storage, and tissue repair.
 
• Parenchyma cells have thin cell walls and large vacuoles, making them versatile in function.
 
 
 
• **Sclerenchyma**
 
 
• It is a type of plant tissue that provides structural support due to its thick, lignified cell walls.
 
• Sclerenchyma cells are usually dead at maturity and include fibers and sclereids.

questions.question: Which of the following carbon compounds is classified as an alcohol?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Propanol**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An alcohol is an organic compound with a hydroxyl group (-OH) attached to a carbon atom.
 
• Propanol, also known as propyl alcohol, has the chemical formula C₃H₇OH.
 
• Propanol is a three-carbon alcohol, specifically a primary alcohol.
 
• It is commonly used as a solvent and in the manufacture of other chemicals.
 
• In contrast, Propanal (an aldehyde), Propanoic (a carboxylic acid), and Propanone (a ketone) do not contain the hydroxyl group characteristic of alcohols.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aldehydes**

 
 
• These compounds have a carbonyl group (C=O) bonded to at least one hydrogen atom.
 
• Propanal is an example of an aldehyde with the formula CH₃CH₂CHO.
 
 
 
• **Carboxylic Acids**
 
 
• These compounds contain a carboxyl group (-COOH).
 
• Propanoic acid, also known as propionic acid, has the formula C₂H₅COOH.
 
 
 
• **Ketones**
 
 
• These compounds have a carbonyl group (C=O) bonded to two carbon atoms.
 
• Propanone, commonly known as acetone, has the formula (CH₃)₂CO.

questions.question: What happens when acid is mixed with water?

options.text: It will increase the concentration of hydronium ions per unit volume.
It will increase the concentration of hydroxyl ions per unit volume.
There will be no effect on the concentration of ions.
It will decrease the concentration of hydronium ions per unit volume.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It will increase the concentration of hydronium ions per unit volume**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When an acid is mixed with water, it dissociates to produce hydronium ions (H₃O⁺).
 
• Hydronium ions are formed when the hydrogen ions (H⁺) from the acid combine with water molecules (H₂O).
 
• This increases the concentration of hydronium ions per unit volume of the solution.
 
• The increase in hydronium ions results in a decrease in the pH of the solution, making it more acidic.
 
• The degree of dissociation and the subsequent increase in hydronium ions depend on the strength of the acid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydroxyl Ions (OH⁻)**

 
 
• When a base is mixed with water, it dissociates to produce hydroxyl ions (OH⁻).
 
• This increases the concentration of hydroxyl ions per unit volume of the solution, making it more basic.
 
 
 
• **Neutralization Reaction**
 
 
• When an acid and a base are mixed, they react to form water and a salt in a neutralization reaction.
 
• This reaction typically results in a decrease in the concentrations of hydronium and hydroxyl ions.
 
 
 
• **pH Scale**
 
 
• The pH scale measures the acidity or basicity of a solution based on the concentration of hydronium ions.
 
• A pH less than 7 indicates an acidic solution, while a pH greater than 7 indicates a basic solution.

questions.question: The kinetic energy possessed by a body of mass 2 kg is 100 J. The velocity of the body will be:
questions.solution:
**Concept:**

 

**Principle of Conservation of Energy:**

 

 
• The principle states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed from one form to another.
 
• In the context of this problem, the potential energy (PE) at the maximum height will be equal to the initial kinetic energy (KE).

**Important terms:**

 
• **Potential Energy (PE):** Energy possessed by a body due to its position or height.

 SI Unit: Joule (J)

 Dimensional Formula: [M L2 T-2]

 
• **Kinetic Energy (KE):** Energy possessed by a body due to its motion.

 SI Unit: Joule (J)

 Dimensional Formula: [M L2 T-2]

 

**Calculation:**

 

**Given:**

Mass of the ball (m) = 2 kg

Kinetic energy (KE) = 100 J

We know,

Kinetic Energy = 1/2 mv²

⇒ 100 = 1/2 × 2 × v²

⇒ 100 = v²

⇒ v = √100 = 10 m/s

**∴ The velocity of the body will be 10 m/s.**

questions.question: Select the process responsible for stability of populations of species.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reproduction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Reproduction** is the biological process by which new individual organisms are produced from their parents.
 
• It is essential for the **continuation and stability of species**, ensuring that populations can be maintained over generations.
 
• There are two main types of reproduction: **asexual and sexual**. Asexual reproduction involves a single organism or cell, while sexual reproduction involves the combination of genetic material from two parents.
 
• Reproduction allows for the **transfer of genetic information** from one generation to the next, which is vital for the survival of a species.
 
• It plays a crucial role in **natural selection and evolution**, as it introduces genetic variation within a population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mutation**

 
 
• Mutations are changes in the DNA sequence that can lead to genetic variation within a population.
 
• They can be beneficial, neutral, or harmful and play a role in the process of evolution.
 
 
 
• **Evolution**
 
 
• Evolution is the process by which different kinds of living organisms develop and diversify from earlier forms over generations.
 
• It involves mechanisms such as natural selection, mutation, gene flow, and genetic drift.
 
 
 
• **Variation**
 
 
• Variation refers to the differences in the genetic makeup and characteristics within and among populations of organisms.
 
• It is essential for the process of natural selection and the overall adaptability of a species.

questions.question: The atomic radius of a hydrogen atom is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10⁻¹⁰ m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The atomic radius is a measure of the size of an atom, typically the mean or typical distance from the nucleus to the boundary of the surrounding cloud of electrons.
 
• Hydrogen is the lightest and most abundant chemical element, consisting of only one proton and one electron.
 
• The atomic radius of a hydrogen atom is approximately 10⁻¹⁰ meters.
 
• This value is also known as 1 angstrom (Å), a common unit of length used in the field of atomic-scale measurements.
 
• Understanding the atomic radius is crucial for studying atomic structures, chemical bonding, and molecular interactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atomic Radii Trends**

 
 
• Atomic radii generally decrease across a period from left to right due to increasing nuclear charge.
 
• Atomic radii increase down a group as additional electron shells are added.
 
 
 
• **Ionic Radius**
 
 
• Ionic radius is the radius of an atom's ion.
 
• Cations are smaller than their parent atoms due to the loss of electron(s) and a resultant increase in nuclear charge.
 
• Anions are larger than their parent atoms due to the gain of electron(s) leading to increased electron-electron repulsion.
 
 
 
• **Van der Waals Radius**
 
 
• This is a measure of the size of an atom or molecule that includes its electron cloud.
 
• It is larger than the covalent radius because it accounts for the space occupied by the electron cloud during non-bonded interactions.

questions.question: What type of reaction occurs when limestone gets converted into quicklime on heating?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Decomposition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Limestone (CaCO₃) decomposes into quicklime (CaO) and carbon dioxide (CO₂) when heated.
 
• This type of reaction is known as a thermal decomposition reaction.
 
• In a decomposition reaction, a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances.
 
• Thermal decomposition usually requires the input of heat energy.
 
• Quicklime (CaO) is widely used in the construction industry and for making cement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Combination Reaction**

 
 
• Involves two or more substances combining to form a single compound.
 
• Example: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O (Formation of water from hydrogen and oxygen).
 
 
 
• **Displacement Reaction**
 
 
• Involves an element displacing another element from a compound.
 
• Example: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu (Zinc displaces copper from copper sulfate).
 
 
 
• **Double Displacement Reaction**
 
 
• Involves the exchange of ions between two compounds to form new compounds.
 
• Example: Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → 2NaCl + BaSO₄ (Sodium sulfate reacts with barium chloride).

questions.question: For current carrying circular loop, the field strength is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**maximum at the centre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The magnetic field strength in a current-carrying circular loop is **maximum at the center** of the loop.
 
• At the center of the loop, the magnetic field lines are **most concentrated**, leading to the highest field strength.
 
• As you move towards the periphery of the loop, the magnetic field strength **decreases**.
 
• The magnetic field strength at the center of a circular loop is given by the formula **B = (μ₀I)/(2R)**, where B is the magnetic field, μ₀ is the permeability of free space, I is the current, and R is the radius of the loop.
 
• This concept is based on the **Biot-Savart law** which describes the magnetic field generated by a steady current.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biot-Savart Law**

 
 
• This law helps in calculating the magnetic field generated by a steady current.
 
• It states that the magnetic field at a point is directly proportional to the current and inversely proportional to the distance from the current element.
 
 
 
• **Right Hand Rule**
 
 
• This rule is used to determine the direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor.
 
• According to this rule, if you point the thumb of your right hand in the direction of the current, the direction in which your fingers curl gives the direction of the magnetic field.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Field Lines**
 
 
• These are imaginary lines used to represent the magnetic field.
 
• The density of these lines indicates the strength of the magnetic field.
 
• Closer lines represent stronger magnetic fields, while lines further apart indicate weaker fields.

questions.question: In the food vacuole of which organism, complex substances are broken down into simpler ones which then diffuse into the cytoplasm?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amoeba**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Amoeba is a single-celled organism that uses a food vacuole for digestion.
 
• The food vacuole in Amoeba engulfs food particles through a process called phagocytosis.
 
• Inside the food vacuole, complex substances are broken down into simpler ones by digestive enzymes.
 
• The simpler substances then diffuse into the cytoplasm to be used by the cell.
 
• This process ensures that Amoeba can efficiently obtain nutrients from its environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plasmodium**

 
 
• Plasmodium is a parasitic protozoan, known for causing malaria in humans.
 
• It has a complex life cycle involving both humans and mosquito hosts.
 
 
 
• **Spirogyra**
 
 
• Spirogyra is a filamentous green alga, known for its spiral chloroplasts.
 
• It reproduces both sexually and asexually through fragmentation and conjugation.
 
 
 
• **Lichen**
 
 
• Lichen is a symbiotic association between a fungus and a photosynthetic partner, usually algae or cyanobacteria.
 
• They are known for their ability to colonize harsh environments, including bare rocks.

questions.question: In which organism does cell division or fission lead to the creation of new individuals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Unicellular organisms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Unicellular organisms are single-celled organisms that perform all necessary functions within one cell.
 
• Cell division in unicellular organisms, such as bacteria and protozoa, is typically asexual and occurs through processes like binary fission or budding.
 
• During binary fission, the cell duplicates its genetic material and divides into two equal-sized daughter cells.
 
• This type of reproduction is efficient and rapid, allowing for quick population growth under favorable conditions.
 
• Unicellular organisms do not require a mate for reproduction, which simplifies the process and ensures the generation of new individuals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multicellular Organisms**

 
 
• In multicellular organisms, cell division is used for growth, development, and repair, rather than creating new individuals.
 
• These organisms reproduce through sexual reproduction, involving the fusion of gametes (sperm and egg cells).
 
 
 
• **Mitosis and Meiosis**
 
 
• Mitosis is a type of cell division resulting in two daughter cells with identical genetic material, used for growth and repair in multicellular organisms.
 
• Meiosis is a specialized form of cell division that produces gametes with half the genetic material, essential for sexual reproduction.
 
 
 
• **Cell Cycle**
 
 
• The cell cycle includes stages of cell growth, DNA replication, and cell division, ensuring the proper distribution of genetic material to daughter cells.
 
• Regulation of the cell cycle is crucial for preventing uncontrolled cell division, which can lead to diseases like cancer.

questions.concept: Periodic Table, Chemistry in Everyday Life
questions.question: Which of following compounds is used as an ingredient in antacids?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium hydrogen carbonate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sodium hydrogen carbonate, also known as baking soda, is commonly used as an ingredient in antacids.
 
• It helps to neutralize stomach acid, providing relief from heartburn and indigestion.
 
• Antacids containing sodium hydrogen carbonate are effective in treating acid reflux and peptic ulcers.
 
• Sodium hydrogen carbonate reacts with hydrochloric acid in the stomach to produce carbon dioxide, water, and salt, reducing acidity.
 
• It is preferred in antacid formulations because it works quickly to relieve symptoms of hyperacidity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydrochloric acid**

 
 
• It is a strong acid produced in the stomach to aid in digestion.
 
• Excess production of hydrochloric acid can lead to conditions like acid reflux and ulcers.
 
 
 
• **Calcium carbonate**
 
 
• It is another compound often used in antacids to neutralize stomach acid.
 
• Calcium carbonate is effective in providing longer-lasting relief compared to sodium hydrogen carbonate.
 
 
 
• **Magnesium hydroxide**
 
 
• Commonly known as milk of magnesia, it is used in antacids to neutralize stomach acid and relieve constipation.
 
• Magnesium hydroxide works by drawing water into the intestines, making it easier to pass stool.

questions.question: Which of the following is the specialised cell that conducts information via electrical impulses from one part of the body to another?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neuron**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Neurons are the fundamental units of the brain and nervous system, responsible for receiving sensory input from the external world.
 
• They conduct information via electrical impulses, known as action potentials, throughout the body.
 
• Neurons connect with each other to form networks that perform various functions such as motor coordination, sensory perception, and cognitive processes.
 
• Each neuron consists of a cell body, dendrites, and an axon, which help in the transmission of electrical signals.
 
• The synapse is the junction between two neurons where information is transmitted from one neuron to another through neurotransmitters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nucleus**

 
 
• The nucleus is the membrane-bound organelle that contains the cell's chromosomes.
 
• It acts as the control center of the cell, regulating gene expression and mediating the replication of DNA during the cell cycle.
 
 
 
• **Dendrite**
 
 
• Dendrites are the branched projections of a neuron that receive electrochemical signals from other neural cells.
 
• They conduct the electrical impulses toward the cell body of the neuron.
 
 
 
• **Axon**
 
 
• The axon is a long, slender projection of a neuron that typically conducts electrical impulses away from the cell body.
